condition.expression: input_mosfet_off AND vcc_present AND NOT en_measured

next_steps.action: Measure the charger IC EN pin and the ACOK output. Most chargers gate the input MOSFET via ACOK (open-drain) and an external inverter; if ACOK is low the MOSFET stays off.

measure.where: Charger EN and ACOK pins (consult datasheet)
measure.expected: ACOK high when adapter is recognised as valid. EN level per datasheet.
measure.safety: ACOK feeds the EC; if the EC is holding the charger off, that is by design (battery-only mode, low current limit).

interpretations.if_result: ACOK high and EN at enabled level
interpretations.then: Charger should be driving the input MOSFET. If the MOSFET gate is still low, suspect the MOSFET driver transistor or the MOSFET itself.

Charger has not declared adapter valid. Check ACIN voltage threshold on the charger datasheet; if ACIN is below threshold the charger will keep the MOSFET off. May indicate an adapter-ID pin issue (middle pin on Dell/HP jacks).
EC is holding the charger off (firmware policy: wrong adapter, battery-only mode, OTP). Read the EC's charger enable register via SMBus if accessible.

next_steps.requires_info_note: Need charger datasheet for EN/ACOK pins and the adapter-ID scheme used by this board.
